documented_impact: Higher heat exposure is associated with more food-insecure households.
fcv_mediator: Household food insecurity and livelihood stress.
possible_consequence: Where other political, economic and security conditions are adverse, food insecurity may contribute to greater conflict risk.
uncertainty: Causal direction and omitted-variable effects remain material.
compact_statement: Extreme heat may raise conflict risk through food insecurity, but available Ethiopia evidence is correlational rather than proof that heat causes conflict. (World Food Programme1)

documented_impact: Pastoralists adjust mobility and other coping strategies.
fcv_mediator: Competition over common water and pasture.
possible_consequence: Increased probability of local intercommunal tension or conflict in some Somali Region settings.
compact_statement: Drought can affect local conflict risk through mobility and governed access to pasture/water; it is not an automatic conflict trigger. (SIPRI7)

documented_impact: Infrastructure, crops, livelihoods and settlements are exposed to flood damage.
fcv_mediator: Displacement, service congestion, lost assets and unequal recovery.
possible_consequence: In fragile or poorly governed settings, these stresses could exacerbate grievances or reduce social cohesion.
uncertainty: No verified source here demonstrates a national flood -> violence causal effect.
compact_statement: Flood impacts may interact with displacement and service deficits, but a conflict consequence remains inferential. (World Bank2)

documented_impact: Conflict exposure is associated with materially higher food poverty in surveyed pastoral/agropastoral communities.
fcv_mediator: Violence, market disruption and household asset/income loss.
possible_consequence: Households affected by conflict may have fewer resources with which to cope with subsequent climate shocks.
uncertainty: Direct effect on specific adaptation outcomes was not measured.
compact_statement: Conflict-associated food poverty plausibly reduces household climate-coping capacity, but the complete adaptation chain has not been directly evaluated. (World Bank2)

climate_pressure: Drought or other climate-related humanitarian stress.
documented_impact: Insecurity creates risks and raises WFP operating costs.
fcv_mediator: Access restrictions, insecurity and increased delivery costs.
possible_consequence: Assistance, recovery and resilience services may reach fewer people, arrive later or cost more.
geographies: Particularly Amhara in current WFP reporting
uncertainty: No quantified causal estimate of lost resilience outcome.
compact_statement: Insecurity demonstrably constrains humanitarian operations; its precise reduction in climate-resilience outcomes is not quantified. (World Food Programme8)

documented_impact: Pastoral dry-season grazing and water access are important to livelihood continuity.
fcv_mediator: Unrecognized communal tenure, expropriation/displacement risk and contested access.
possible_consequence: Poorly governed land change may heighten livelihood vulnerability and potentially aggravate local fragility.
institutions: Formal land administration and customary institutions
resilience_factors: Recognition of communal rights and locally grounded customary governance
compact_statement: Institutions governing land and seasonal access can mediate whether climate stress becomes a livelihood or fragility problem. (World Bank2)

documented_impact: Drought insurance/cash can help households maintain livestock or meet needs.
fcv_mediator: Reduced need for drought-driven mobility and competition.
possible_consequence: Intercommunal conflict risk may fall where mobility-related resource competition is a relevant conflict mechanism.
uncertainty: Severe drought still generated migration; peace effect not rigorously estimated.
compact_statement: Insurance has a plausible peace-supporting pathway, but evidence is mixed and programme targeting can generate its own tensions. (SIPRI7)

climate_pressure: Drought, erosion and land degradation interacting with climate variability.
documented_impact: Evaluated SLM interventions improved land-restoration indicators.
fcv_mediator: Distribution of access, grazing restrictions and livelihood compensation.
possible_consequence: Well-designed restoration can increase resilience; poorly designed closures can increase livestock-keeper vulnerability and potentially create grievances.
uncertainty: Evidence concerns evaluated watersheds, not all restoration programmes.
compact_statement: Adaptation can restore ecosystems while producing distributional harm if livelihood access is ignored. (Independent Evaluation Group13) ---
